title: Azure SQL Backup, High Availability, and Resilience
description: Learn how Azure SQL automatically backs up data and provides high availability through zone-redundant and geo-redundant configurations.

data.text: Azure SQL Database is a PaaS service, so Microsoft handles backups, patching, and high availability automatically. You configure the **service tier** and **high availability** options, and Azure ensures your data is protected and your database stays online.

Azure SQL takes full backups weekly, differential backups every 12-24 hours, and transaction log backups every 5-10 minutes. Backups are stored in RA-GRS storage by default, so they survive regional outages. Retention ranges from 7 to 35 days, and you can extend it with long-term retention (LTR).

data.title: Configure Long-Term Retention with Azure CLI
data.code:
az sql db ltr-policy set \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --server sqlserver-demo \
  --database AppDb \
  --weekly-retention P12W

data.title: Restores Are Not Instant
data.text: Point-in-time restore time depends on database size. Large databases may take hours to restore. Plan DR runbooks and test them before you need them.

data.title: Exercise: Perform a Point-in-Time Restore
data.description: Restore a database to a specific point in time and verify the data.
steps: Insert a row into a test table and note the current time.
Use the Azure Portal to restore the database to a new database 5 minutes earlier.
Query the restored database and confirm the row exists.
Clean up the restored database when finished.
data.expectedOutcome: A restored database showing the state of data at the chosen point in time.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure SQL automatically backs up data with full, differential, and log backups.
Point-in-time restore lets you recover from user errors within the retention window.
Auto-failover groups provide cross-region disaster recovery with automatic failover.
Long-term retention supports compliance requirements beyond the default window.
data.takeaway: Azure SQL handles the heavy lifting of backup and HA, but you must configure policies and test recovery.
